subject: Hybrid onramp strategy for FinPort: front-door, transit, fallback
messages:
From: Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@finport.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ingress options for FinPort (PCI scope, multi-region)

Markus / team,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. FinPort is moving to pilot Redwood Private for transaction scoring. We have two constraints up front: (1) PCI-in-scope nodes must not traverse the public internet outside of our control, and (2) we expect steady 1-1.5 Gbps egress from our primary DC with occasional spikes to 3 Gbps.

Can you outline tradeoffs between VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and a site-to-site VPN for a setup where we want low-latency synchronous requests for fraud checks (p99 goal < 60ms) and a fallback that tolerates higher latency? Also curious about operational concerns (routing, MTU, failover behavior).

Attached: short diagram from our netops team (not attached here for security) — happy to share a formal attachment if useful.

Best,
Mike Thompson
Head of Engineering, FinPort

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@finport.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ingress options for FinPort (PCI scope, multi-region)

Mike — thanks, this is helpful. I sketched a pragmatic three-tier onramp approach below and attached a quick cost/ops spreadsheet (connectivity-costs.xlsx):

1) Front-door (low-latency, high-assurance): AWS PrivateLink to a Redwood NLB per-region for PCI-scoped traffic. Advantages: 1) traffic stays within provider backbone, 2) no cross-account VPC-route leakage, 3) easier to lock down via SGs. Tradeoffs: per-AZ ENI limits and NAT/MTU considerations for large payloads.

2) Transit peering (high-throughput): Dedicated VPC peering or Transit Gateway peering for non-PCI high-throughput calls (batch, embed pipelines). Advantages: simpler path, lower cost at high sustained throughput. Tradeoffs: routing complexity, careful control of route table propagation, L4-only isolation without additional controls.

3) Backup tunnel: a managed site-to-site VPN (preferably AZ-diverse, BGP-based) as an automated fallback with health checks. Advantages: provides last-resort reachability and a familiar procurement model. Tradeoffs: higher latency and jitter; less deterministic for p99s.

Operational notes:
- MTU: PrivateLink ENIs often require an MSS clamp; plan for 1400 MTU on the customer side to avoid fragmentation.
- Failover: use active/active PrivateLink across regions for active path, with route preference configured for peering on stable high-throughput traffic.
- Auditability: ensure flow logs on both sides and token-aware ingress so you can trace per-request.

Can Kimberley and Rishi validate the assumptions below (MTU, perf baseline, and ENI limits)? Mike — if this looks acceptable I can turn it into a Mutual Action Plan for procurement and NetOps to sign.

Attachment: connectivity-costs.xlsx (simple cost model).

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ingress options for FinPort (PCI scope, multi-region)

Filtering in my notes — I ran a quick checklist against AWS constraints and FinPort's requirements:

- ENI scaling: PrivateLink requires one ENI per AZ per endpoint. For heavy concurrency, customer must pre-warm or use multiple endpoints across AZs to distribute connections.
- Connection churn: short-lived TCP connections (common for small sync RPCs) can exhaust ephemeral port ranges on the ENI. Recommend connection pooling or keep-alives from FinPort app layer.
- MTU/MSS: If FinPort uses jumbo frames internally, ensure MSS clamp at the egress NAT; otherwise you'll see fragmentation and latency spikes. Recommend setting MTU to 1500 -> clamp to 1400 for PrivateLink.
- Route propagation: peering/transit setups are simpler for route control but do not provide per-service security boundaries. If FinPort needs strict separation, PrivateLink is better.

Attachment: mk-privatelink-notes.pdf — I captured the ENI scaling math and a small runbook for failover detection (health checks + endpoint deregistration pattern).

Operational ask: can we get FinPort's expected connection churn profile (avg connections/sec, avg session duration) so we can size endpoints and recommend pooling settings?

Kimberly
Senior Network Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@finport.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T16:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ingress options for FinPort (PCI scope, multi-region)

Quick performance note from our microbench runs (attached latency-bench-120s.csv):
- PrivateLink -> avg 18ms, p99 42ms (single AZ endpoint, TCP persist).
- VPC peering (same-region) -> avg 12ms, p99 30ms.
- VPN (managed, BGP) -> avg 75ms, p99 200ms (visible jitter on rekeys).

Observations: PrivateLink meets your p99 goal in our tests with persistent connections but is vulnerable to ENI port exhaustion under high churn. Peering gives slightly better latency and is more predictable for sustained high throughput. VPN should be explicitly treated as a fallback lane and included in the runbook for failover testing only.

Operational recommendation:
- Primary: PrivateLink for PCI traffic with two endpoints in different AZs + connection pooling + early SYN retries.
- Bulk traffic: Transit peering for throughput.
- Fallback: S2S VPN with automated traffic-shift playbook and synthetic traffic monitoring.

I'll sync with NetOps to quantify the egress NAT window and ephemeral port counts — attaching raw bench CSV.

Rishi
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

—Mike

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Ingress options for FinPort (PCI scope, multi-region)

SG — I'll produce a MAP and a short pilot checklist by EOD tomorrow. Preliminary answers / action items:

Decisions (proposed):
- Use PrivateLink (interface endpoints) as the PCI front-door anchored in FinPort security account. We'll support cross-account endpoints (standard AWS model) and provide a per-region NLB in our serving VPCs.
- Use Transit Gateway peering for non-PCI high-throughput traffic between FinPort VPCs and Redwood transit VPC.
- Provision a managed BGP VPN as the third-tier fallback with automated health-based failover.

Action items:
- FinPort NetOps: share connections/sec and avg session duration (Mike).
- Redwood NetOps (Kimberly): produce ENI scaling guidance and a small pre-warm script; include MTU/MSS clamp recommendations.
- Redwood SRE (Rishi): finalize bench results and define synthetic tests for p99 monitoring.
- Procurement: will work with procurement@finport.com on terms and PO cadence once MAP is shared.

I will drop the MAP and a short runbook link here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/finport/onramp-proposal and update the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FP-2026-2093.

If everyone agrees, I'll mark this as the recommended architecture and start the pilot kickoff thread.

Thanks all —
Markus Klein
